005930 KS · Semiconductors 
Samsung Electronics 
Disappointment already priced in 
Investment points and valuation 
We lower our 12-month target price for Samsung Electronics (SEC) to W78,000 (from 
W80,000), as we reduced our target P/B to 1.2x (from 1.3x). While a 1.3x P/B is not an 
overly ambitious target, SEC’s decision to write off HBM inventory raises questions 
about whether the related manufacturing facilities, technological capabilities, and 
intangible assets are working in full synergy to generate meaningful leverage.  
SEC’s supply of 12 -layer HBM3E to North America’s leading GPU maker has been 
delayed until after 3Q25. The memory market —which was previously centered on 
commoditized products, allowing all players to produce and compete on cost—has 
evolved to a point where only a few manufacturers can deliver advanced products. This 
shift in the competitive landscape has enabled leading players to adopt a more 
conservative capex approach, reducing uncertainty and maximizing profitability.  
According to the market research firm IDC, HBM bit growth in 2026 is projected at 
around 30%, below the consensus of around 40%. And notably, the projected bit share 
of HBM4 is high, at 24%, suggesting a relatively short product life cycle for HBM3E. 
Against this backdrop, we believe SEC needs to provide investors with a realistic and 
predictable HBM business road map/guidance.  
Nevertheless, we maintain our Buy rating, as SEC’s continued robust positioning in 
smartphones, flexible display panels, and commodity memory chips should provide 
firm downside support at a P/B of 1x. Also, the recently announced W3.9tr buyback 
should have a positive effect on investor demand, while potential share cancellations in 
the future should enhance shareholder returns.  
In the global accelerator industry, major buyers currently rely on an unprecedentedly 
concentrated supply chain centered on just three companies. And the only viable path 
for diversifying the supply chain is for SEC to regain competitiveness. We believe SEC is 
fully committed to th is goal, having kept its R&D investments (as a percentage of 
revenue) elevated over the past six quarters. As such, we estimate SEC’s HBM market 
share will reach 26% for 2026 and 35% for 2027. 
SEC announced preliminary 2Q25 revenue of W74.1tr (-6.4% QoQ) and operating profit 
of W4.6tr (-31.8% QoQ). By division, we estimate operating profit at W 3.3tr for DX, 
W0.4tr for DS, W0.4tr for Samsung Display, and W0.4tr for Harman (final results to be 
announced on Jul. 31). While revenue was likely broadly in line with expectations, we 
estimate the DS unit sharply missed our previous operating profit estimate (W2.3tr).
